## `idx`

```text
idx-cli is a Rust command-line tool for Indonesian stock market (IDX) analysis.
It supports quote lookup, historical data, local caching, and output formats for both humans and AI agents.

Usage: idx [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  stocks       Stock data and analysis
  config       Manage configuration
  cache        Manage local cache
  ownership    Ownership intelligence (bootstrap with `ownership sync`)
  stockbit     Your Stockbit session (opt-in: order book, live quotes)
  completions  Generate shell completions
  version      Show idx-cli version
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `idx stocks`

```text
Stock data and analysis

Usage: idx stocks [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  quote        Get real-time stock quotes
  intraday     Today's session price by the minute (Stockbit)
  orderbook    Order book depth and foreign flow (Stockbit login)
  history      Get historical OHLC data
  technical    Run technical analysis on a stock
  growth       Run growth analysis on a stock
  valuation    Run valuation analysis on a stock
  risk         Run risk analysis on a stock
  fundamental  Run full fundamental analysis on a stock
  broker       Which brokers bought and sold a stock
  bandar       Bandarmology: is buying more concentrated than selling
  flow         Foreign buying and selling of a stock, session by session
  profile      Get company profile
  financials   Get financial statements
  earnings     Get earnings report
  sentiment    Get crowd sentiment
  insights     Get AI insights
  news         Get stock news
  screen       MSN screener
  compare      Compare fundamentals across stocks
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>      Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped] [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]
      --no-color             Disable colored output
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential output
  -v, --verbose...           Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)
      --provider <PROVIDER>  Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn] [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]
      --offline              Run without network requests
      --no-cache             Bypass local cache
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

### `idx stocks quote`

```text
Get real-time stock quotes

Usage: idx stocks quote [OPTIONS] <SYMBOLS>...

Arguments:
  <SYMBOLS>...  One or more symbols, comma-separated or space-separated; `-` reads them from stdin

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>      Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped] [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]
      --no-color             Disable colored output
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential output
  -v, --verbose...           Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)
      --provider <PROVIDER>  Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn] [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]
      --offline              Run without network requests
      --no-cache             Bypass local cache
  -h, --help                 Print help

Examples:
  idx stocks quote BBCA
  idx stocks quote BBCA,BBRI,BMRI
  idx -o json stocks quote BBCA
  echo BBCA BBRI | idx stocks quote -
  idx --provider stockbit stocks quote BBCA   # with bid/offer while the market is open
```

### `idx stocks intraday`

```text
Today's session of one IDX stock or index, by the minute, from Stockbit's public page (no login): the quote, the best bid/offer while the market is open, a sparkline, and the last minutes. Delayed at least 10 minutes per Stockbit's terms; prices only, no per-minute volume. A stock that did not trade has no minutes, which is not an error. Indices use Yahoo's tickers (^JKSE, ^JKLQ45) or Stockbit's (IHSG, LQ45).

Usage: idx stocks intraday [OPTIONS] <SYMBOL>

Arguments:
  <SYMBOL>
          Single ticker symbol (e.g. BBCA)

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  idx stocks intraday BBCA
  idx stocks intraday ^JKSE
  idx -o json stocks intraday BBCA | jq '.points[-1]'
```

### `idx stocks orderbook`

```text
The order book of one IDX stock from your own Stockbit session (`idx stockbit login`): bid and offer levels with lots and queued orders, the session's OHLC, volume, value and foreign buy, sell and net. Outside trading it is the book as the market left it, and the output says so.

Usage: idx stocks orderbook [OPTIONS] <SYMBOL>

Arguments:
  <SYMBOL>
          Single ticker symbol (e.g. BBCA)

Options:
      --depth <DEPTH>
          Price levels per side (1-50)

          [default: 10]

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  idx stocks orderbook BBCA
  idx stocks orderbook BBRI --depth 5
  idx -o json stocks orderbook TLKM | jq '.offers[0]'
```

### `idx stocks broker`

```text
Which brokers bought and sold a stock: the top 10 buyers and top 10 sellers by lots, with value and average price, from Indo Premier (IPOT). End of day: IDX does not show broker codes during trading. Without dates, the latest session with trades.

Usage: idx stocks broker [OPTIONS] <SYMBOL>

Arguments:
  <SYMBOL>
          Single ticker symbol (e.g. BBCA)

Options:
      --date <DATE>
          One session, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest session with trades

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --from <FROM>
          First session of a range, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 366 days)

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

      --to <TO>
          Last session of the range, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today

      --investor <INVESTOR>
          Whose trades to count

          Possible values:
          - all:      Every trade
          - foreign:  Trades by foreign investors only
          - domestic: Trades by domestic investors only

          [default: all]

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --board <BOARD>
          Which board's trades to count; `regular` leaves out negotiated block trades

          Possible values:
          - all:        Every board
          - regular:    Regular market (RG), the continuous order book
          - cash:       Cash market (TN)
          - negotiated: Negotiated market (NG): pre-arranged block trades

          [default: all]

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  idx stocks broker BBCA
  idx stocks broker BBCA --date 2026-10-16
  idx stocks broker BBCA --from 2026-10-12 --to 2026-10-16 --board regular
  idx -o json stocks broker BBCA --investor foreign
```

### `idx stocks bandar`

```text
Bandarmology from the broker summary: the top 1, 3, 5 and 10 buyers' value against the same number of sellers', as a share of value traded, with a signal from big accumulation to big distribution. Several symbols give a screen ranked by the headline tier (at most 100, one request each). `--investor foreign|domestic` weighs that side's buyers against its buying and its sellers against its selling (needs `--board all`). A heuristic over end-of-day broker codes, not advice.

Usage: idx stocks bandar [OPTIONS] <SYMBOLS>...

Arguments:
  <SYMBOLS>...
          One or more symbols, comma-separated or space-separated; `-` reads them from stdin

Options:
      --date <DATE>
          One session, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest session with trades

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --from <FROM>
          First session of a range, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 366 days)

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

      --to <TO>
          Last session of the range, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today

      --investor <INVESTOR>
          Whose trades to count

          Possible values:
          - all:      Every trade
          - foreign:  Trades by foreign investors only
          - domestic: Trades by domestic investors only

          [default: all]

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --board <BOARD>
          Which board's trades to count; `regular` leaves out negotiated block trades

          Possible values:
          - all:        Every board
          - regular:    Regular market (RG), the continuous order book
          - cash:       Cash market (TN)
          - negotiated: Negotiated market (NG): pre-arranged block trades

          [default: all]

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --top <TOP>
          Tier behind the headline signal: 1, 3, 5 or 10 brokers per side

          [default: 5]

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  idx stocks bandar BBCA
  idx stocks bandar BBCA --from 2026-10-12 --to 2026-10-16 --top 3
  idx stocks bandar BBCA,BBRI,BMRI,TLKM
  idx stocks screen --filter high-volume | jq -r '.[].symbol' | idx stocks bandar -
```

### `idx stocks flow`

```text
Foreign buying and selling of a stock, session by session, end of day. By default from Indo Premier (IPOT): foreign buy, sell and net value across all boards and foreign investors' share of trading, two plain requests per session. `--source idx` reads IDX's own trading summary instead: exact foreign share counts, the close and the share traded outside the regular board, one request per session to idx.co.id, which needs curl-impersonate and a network IDX's Cloudflare lets through.

Usage: idx stocks flow [OPTIONS] <SYMBOL>

Arguments:
  <SYMBOL>
          Single ticker symbol (e.g. BBCA)

Options:
      --days <DAYS>
          Latest sessions to show (default 10, at most 60)

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --from <FROM>
          First session of a range, YYYY-MM-DD (at most 92 days)

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

      --to <TO>
          Last session of the range, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today

      --source <SOURCE>
          Where the figures come from

          Possible values:
          - ipot: Indo Premier's broker summary: foreign buy, sell and net value across all boards, two plain requests per session. Figures of a million and more are rounded to one decimal
          - idx:  IDX's own trading summary: exact foreign share counts, close and the non-regular share, regular board. Needs curl-impersonate and a network IDX's Cloudflare lets through

          [default: ipot]

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  idx stocks flow BBCA
  idx stocks flow BBCA --days 20
  idx stocks flow BBCA --from 2026-10-01 --to 2026-10-16
  idx stocks flow BBCA --source idx
  idx -o json stocks flow BBCA | jq '.foreign_net_value'
```

## `idx config`

```text
Manage configuration in ~/.config/idx/config.toml (or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/idx/config.toml).

Results print as plain text, even when piped, so `$(idx config path)` works in scripts. Ask for JSON with `-o json`, `IDX_OUTPUT=json`, or `general.output = "json"`.

Usage: idx config [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init  Create default configuration file
  get   Get a configuration value by key
  set   Set a configuration value by key
  path  Print configuration file path
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Keys:
  general.provider, general.history_provider, general.exchange, general.output,
  general.color, cache.quote_ttl, cache.fundamental_ttl, ownership.db_path,
  ownership.snapshot_manifest

Examples:
  idx config init
```

## `idx ownership`

```text
Ownership intelligence (KSEI + Bing).

Preferred bootstrap path:
  1. Run `idx ownership sync` to install or refresh a maintained SQLite snapshot.
  2. If no snapshot manifest is available, run `idx ownership discover` and then `idx ownership import --url <pdf-url>`.
  3. Local `.xlsx`, `.pdf`, `.zip`, and `.txt` imports remain available for manual or fallback workflows.

Usage: idx ownership [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  discover       Discover the latest IDX-hosted ownership report URLs
  import         Import ownership data directly from source files
  sync           Install or refresh a maintained ownership SQLite snapshot
  ticker         Show all holders for a ticker (KSEI + Bing combined)
  entity         Show all holdings for an entity across tickers
  search         Search entities by name or KSEI alias
  cross-holders  Rank entities by cross-ownership breadth
  concentration  Rank tickers by ownership concentration
  flow           Show Bing institutional flow for a ticker
  changes        Diff two KSEI releases
  graph          Ownership network graph
  resolve        Manual entity resolution workflow
  releases       List imported KSEI releases
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  idx ownership sync
  idx ownership sync --manifest /path/to/ownership-snapshot-manifest.json
  idx ownership discover --limit 1
  idx ownership import --url <pdf-url>
  idx ownership releases
```

### `idx ownership discover`

```text
Discover the latest IDX-hosted ownership report URLs

Usage: idx ownership discover [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --family <FAMILY>      Report family to discover: above1 (default), all, above5, or investor-type [default: above1]
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>      Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped] [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]
      --limit <LIMIT>        Maximum number of discovered report URLs to print [default: 6]
      --no-color             Disable colored output
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential output
  -v, --verbose...           Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)
      --provider <PROVIDER>  Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn] [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]
      --offline              Run without network requests
      --no-cache             Bypass local cache
  -h, --help                 Print help

Examples:
  idx ownership discover --limit 1
  idx ownership discover --family all --limit 6

Use this when no snapshot manifest is available and you need a direct XLSX or PDF URL for `idx ownership import --url`.
```

### `idx ownership import`

```text
Import ownership data directly from source files.

Prefer `idx ownership sync` for normal bootstrap/update flows. Use `import` when you need a direct PDF import from IDX discovery output, a local PDF, or a local KSEI archive fallback file.

Usage: idx ownership import [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --url <URL>
          Direct URL to a remote above-1% XLSX or PDF, typically from `ownership discover`

      --file <FILE>
          Path to a local ownership file: above-1% XLSX or PDF (primary), ZIP/TXT archive (fallback)

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

      --fetch-bing <FETCH_BING>
          Fetch Bing institutional data for these symbols

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

      --force
          Re-import even if the release SHA-256 has already been seen

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  idx ownership import --url <pdf-url-from-discover>
  idx ownership import --file /path/to/peng-2026-08-00017-satu-persen.xlsx
  idx ownership import --file /path/to/ksei.pdf
  idx ownership import --file /path/to/BalanceposEfek20260227.zip
```

### `idx ownership sync`

```text
Install or refresh a maintained ownership SQLite snapshot.

This is the normal bootstrap/update path for ownership data.

Manifest lookup order:
  1. `--manifest`
  2. `IDX_OWNERSHIP_SNAPSHOT_MANIFEST`
  3. `ownership.snapshot_manifest` in config

Usage: idx ownership sync [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --manifest <MANIFEST>
          Snapshot manifest location (URL or local path). If omitted, idx falls back through env/config and then the published default URL

  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --force
          Replace the local DB even when it is already current or newer than the snapshot

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  idx ownership sync
  idx ownership sync --manifest /path/to/ownership-snapshot-manifest.json
  IDX_OWNERSHIP_SNAPSHOT_MANIFEST=https://example.com/latest.json idx ownership sync

If none of the above are set, `ownership sync` falls back to the built-in published manifest URL.
```

## `idx stockbit`

```text
Your own Stockbit session, for `stocks orderbook`, live `--provider stockbit` quotes and Stockbit daily history. Opt-in and personal: idx uses your account's tokens, stored in the config directory with owner-only permissions, and never logs them. Stockbit rotates the refresh token on every refresh, so a browser sharing the session is logged out once idx refreshes: log in through a separate browser profile for idx. Stockbit's terms allow personal, non-commercial use.

Usage: idx stockbit [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  login   Store a session pasted on stdin and check it with Stockbit
  status  Show whether a session is stored and when its tokens expire
  logout  Delete the stored session
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]

          [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]

      --no-color
          Disable colored output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn]

          [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]

      --offline
          Run without network requests

      --no-cache
          Bypass local cache

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  idx stockbit login                 # paste the credentialStorage cookie
  pbpaste | idx stockbit login
  idx stockbit status
  idx stockbit logout
```

### `idx stockbit login`

```text
Reads, on stdin, the value of stockbit.com's `credentialStorage` cookie (in a logged-in browser: DevTools, Application, Cookies, https://stockbit.com) or a refresh token, stores it, and checks it with one request. Servers can set IDX_STOCKBIT_REFRESH_TOKEN instead.

Usage: idx stockbit login [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped]
```

```text
Usage: idx version [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>      Output format [default: auto = table on a terminal, json when piped] [possible values: auto, table, json, jsonl]
      --no-color             Disable colored output
  -q, --quiet                Suppress non-essential output
  -v, --verbose...           Increase verbosity (-v, -vv)
      --provider <PROVIDER>  Market data provider [default: general.provider, else msn] [possible values: yahoo, msn, stockbit]
      --offline              Run without network requests
      --no-cache             Bypass local cache
  -h, --help                 Print help
```
